extracted.intended_audience: science journalists, authors, editors, producers, institutional communicators, students, and others who write or produce material intended to inform the public about science, health, engineering, and technology
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational standards and principles NASW sets for science writers and the association itself, covering professional interests, ethics, press freedom, inclusion, and expectations of journalistic quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster dissemination of accurate information
rubrics_metrics.description: Charter to 'foster the dissemination of accurate information regarding science through all media normally devoted to informing the public.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NASW's foundational purpose is to promote accurate public communication of science across media; accuracy and public-oriented dissemination are primary evaluative goals for members' work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote professional interests and fair compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: NASW promotes the professional interests of science writers nationally and globally, plays an active role in supporting efforts to ensure writers are paid for their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The association advocates for conditions (e.g., pay practices, contracts) that support sustainable professional careers for science writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate for copyright protections for writers
rubrics_metrics.description: NASW advocates for copyright protections for writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protecting writers' intellectual property rights is an organizational priority; activities may include advocacy, policy engagement, and member support around copyright issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defend press freedom and access to scientific information
rubrics_metrics.description: NASW fights for the free flow of science news and actively promotes press freedom while facilitating efforts to preserve and improve access to information related to science and scientific research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for open access to research reporting, opposition to censorship, and efforts to remove barriers to information are core criteria by which NASW evaluates threats to science communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to diversity, equity, accessibility, and inclusion (DEAI)
rubrics_metrics.description: NASW is committed to diversity, equity, accessibility, and inclusion and values these principles for how they enrich the profession; this commitment applies to every aspect of NASW and extends to the broader field of science writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NASW states that full representation of storytellers, subjects, and sources is necessary to identify and communicate the full range of science stories; DEAI considerations should inform story selection, sourcing, and organizational practices. The page lists protected and covered dimensions (race, ethnicity, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, physical ability, nationality, age, socioeconomic status, belief).

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero tolerance for harassment, discrimination, or incivility
rubrics_metrics.description: NASW states 'We do not tolerate harassment, discrimination, or incivility.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional conduct expectations for members and participants are explicit; respectful behavior and the absence of harassment/discrimination are required norms even if specific enforcement procedures are described elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uphold the highest standards of journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Members 'foster the interpretation of science and its meaning to society, in keeping with the highest standards of journalism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work and conduct should reflect rigorous reporting, accuracy, ethical sourcing, transparency, and other generally accepted journalistic standards as applied to science communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support community and craft improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Founding purpose: provide a forum to join forces to improve their craft and encourage conditions that promote good science writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NASW emphasizes professional development, community-building, and mutual support as criteria for evaluating member activities and the association's programs.
